FORM: After losing 12 of their previous 13, the Broncos produced a remarkable 34-30 comeback win over a desperate Canberra side at GIO Stadium last Friday.
The Storm have lost four of their last five but followed up a 42-20 thrashing of Manly in Perth with a 22-14 home loss to heavyweight Penrith last week.
INS AND OUTS: The Broncos are unchanged, with Michael Maguire controversially denying Adam Reynolds an NRL farewell.

KEY STAT: The Storm boast a 32-13 record at Suncorp Stadium but have won only one of their last five at the venue.
VERDICT: The Broncos’ brave fightback in Canberra really came out of nowhere, but can they back it up to snap an eye-watering eight-match losing streak at Suncorp Stadium? The bubbling controversy over Reynolds’ non-selection doesn’t help.

items.body_excerpt:
Jett Cleary is set to make his NRL debut after the Warriors ’ halves crisis deepened, with a fourth playmaker injured on the eve of the finals.
In a double blow, the Warriors confirmed on Saturday Chanel Harris-Tavita had suffered a hamstring strain and Te Maire Martin would also not return against Newcastle.
Harris-Tavita had effectively been the last Warriors half left standing, with Tanah Boyd already ruled out for the season and Luke Metcalf also hurt.

The Warriors are confident the pair will train fully in the lead up to next Saturday’s final-round clash with Manly, and stressed the decision was precautionary.
The club’s run to the top of the NRL ladder has come despite the ongoing injury woes, with Sunday to mark the ninth spine combination used by Andrew Webster this year.
Even with all that, wins in the Warriors’ last two games will ensure a top-two finish and the chance to avoid travel and stay in Auckland until grand final week.
Martin has not played since he tore his hamstring in round 22, while Harris-Tavita is understood to have pulled up sore at training this week.
It means the youngest Cleary will debut for the table-topping club on Sunday in Auckland, with Luke Hansen playing his third NRL match alongside him at five-eighth.
Combined, the duo will make for the least experienced halves pairing in Warriors history.
They will also be the least experienced in the NRL since Jack Cogger and Brock Lamb at Newcastle in 2016.
The pair, who are both Penrith juniors, at least have the advantage of playing together in NSW Cup over the past two years.
Cleary joined the Warriors in 2025, and came off the bench in last year’s State Cup final at Accor Stadium on NRL grand final day, with his brother Nathan and father Ivan among the family in attendance.
The 21-year-old has has since been released to return to Penrith next year for Ivan’s last year as an NRL coach.
The Warriors will also have Luke Laulilii start on the wing for the first time after his mid-season transfer from Wests Tigers, as a result of Dallin Watene-Zelezniak’s broken shoulder last week.
Watene-Zelezniak is expected to return for the finals, as is second-rower Jackson Ford after his best ever season was halted by a pec injury in June.

Jett Cleary will make his long-awaited Warriors debut against the Knights on Sunday.
Cleary will make his debut paired with Luke Hanson. On Saturday afternoon, the team said it was the least experienced halves combination in Warriors history.
They take the place of the halves pairing of Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita.
"It has been decided not to risk the established halves this week," the Warriors said.
"Martin was named on Tuesday to return from a hamstring complaint which kept him out of the last three matches against Penrith, Brisbane and South Sydney.
"However, he has been omitted tomorrow as has Harris-Tavita who has a minor hamstring issue. Both will train fully next week to line up in the final regular season match against Manly Warringah on Saturday (September 5).
It had been looking highly unlikely Jett - the son of former Warrior Ivan Cleary, and younger brother of of four-time premiership winner Nathan - would ever make his first grade debut with the Warriors after being granted an early release from his contract on compassionate grounds.
It allows him to return to Australia at the end of the 2026 season.
Quiet force behind Warriors' rise
While Leka Halasima will happily charge headfirst into an NRL defence line, when it comes to fronting the cameras, he is quick to turn the other way.
The NZ Warriors superstar has been notorious for avoiding media since exploding onto the rugby league scene, admitting as much during his one and only appearance in front of journalists this season.
"I've been hiding," he said with a smile.
Though uncomfortable with the spotlight, Halasima plays a big role behind the scenes at the club.
Teammate Demitric Vaimauga said 'Leka the Wrecker' was equally impressive off the pitch.
"There's way more to Leka than his special plays and his quietness, his shyness," the Warriors second-rower said. "He's a real intelligent guy."
After a mid-season slump , Vaimauga said Halasima took it upon himself to inspire his fellow rookies and get things back on track.
"We have a little group chat, Leka started it. We weren't going so well in the middle of the season, we had a little rough patch, so Leka brought us all together, fired us up and just reminded us how how special it is to be on the the big stage all together.
"It was, like, just remember why we're here, what got us here, go back to our superpowers, our strengths and just play footy."
Vaimauga said the pep talk was the catalyst for the younger members in the squad rediscovering their form.
"There was a stretch there where Jakey [Jacob Laban] was playing probably the best footy for us. Ali [Leiataua] found his groove again, and I just felt most of us young boys stepped up and were playing some good footy, which has taken us to where we are now."

Manly Warringah Sea Eagles have defeated St George Illawarra Dragons 44-10 in Round 26 of the NRL Telstra Premiership to keep their finals hopes alive.

Manly’s 500th win at 4 Pines Park arrived six days after the club’s 1000th win, achieved in Newcastle last weekend.
It was also a perfect send-off for departing players Reuben Garrick and Nathan Brown, who will both be moving on after this season.
Garrick scored one of five first half tries while Brown, playing his 200th game in his third and final season at Manly, as always was full of energy.
Bouncing around like a pinball, it was a burst from Brown which put Jake Trbojevic in the clear in the lead up to the first of Saab’s two first half tries.
Manly scored the opening try of the match in the 7th minute when five-eighth Clayton Faulalo floated a long ball onto the chest of an unmarked Lehi Hopoate in the northwestern corner.
Saab then went back-to-back, scoring two tries in four minutes, both coming off short cross-field kicks from Jamal Fogarty.
Manly found themselves up 16-0 after 20 minutes and the points continued to flow, with Saab again in the thick of the action.
This time he turned provider after being put away by Tom Trbojevic down the eastern touchline. Saab found Garrick on his inside who crossed for his 98th career try.
Up 22-0, Turbo was next across for Manly as Faulalo continued to look right at home in the No.6 jersey. Shaping inside, he gave to Turbo on the outside, who split defenders to score in the northwestern corner.
With Fogarty unable to convert, Manly led 26-0 at the break, and looked well on track for back-to-back wins, and a second win over the Dragons this season.
It took about 10 minutes into the second half for Manly to score again, extending their lead to 32-0. Faulalo was again involved, cashing in on a Dragons’ mistake to send Josh Feledy in for a try from close range.
After scoring a 16-minute hat-trick in Newcastle last week, this was his first try at 4 Pines Park.
After a few try assists Faulalo bagged one for himself a few minutes later before being forced from the field for a HIA.
He showed a clean set of heels to race 70 metres after swooping on yet another Dragons’ error.
Many were up 36-0 with a little over 20 minutes remaining when Faulalo copped a heavy knock while defending. He passed the inspection but remained off the field.
His exit saw the long-awaited introduction to the NRL for Onitoni Large. The 19-year-old five-eighth entered the game with a high-five from Tom Trbojevic, and a big cheer from the grandstands, becoming Sea Eagle #676.
Large had barely touched a ball before Manly were in for try number eight. A trademark Haumole Olakau’atu try from about 25 metres out sent Manly ahead 40-0 on the hour mark.
The final stretch was a mere formality with the Dragons adding a couple of consolation tries, either side of Hopoate’s second for the match.
With just under six minutes until full time, Hopoate collected a neat ball on the short side from Feledy to score his team’s ninth and final try of the evening.
It was night to savour for the Sea Eagles, past and present.
With the 1996 Premiership-winning team watching on, there to celebrate their Grand Final victory over the Dragons 30 years ago, it was a tremendous way for this year's team to keep their finals hopes alive.
Next up is a clash against the Warriors in Auckland next Saturday in the final round of the regular season.

NRL Match Preview: Back home chasing top two finish
Sitting near the top of the ladder, the One New Zealand Warriors have it all to play for against the Knights on Sunday with a top two finish giving them a home final at Go Media Stadium.
Despite a number of injury set-backs, the Warriors have taken the challenges in their stride this season and will be hoping to keep winning momentum rolling into and throughout the finals.
Next-player-up has been their mindset this year, but their latest loss - winger Dallin Watene-Zelezniak - will be keenly felt, with the 'flying mullet' in rare try-scoring form. He even managed to cross for one last week despite it later being revealed he had a broken collarbone.
And now they're without senior halves Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita for this contest with debutant Jett Cleary and 2026 rookie Luke Hanson called up.
The Knights have headed across the ditch no doubt still smarting from a poor loss last week against Manly, who thoroughly out-pointed and out-enthused them 44-24 despite the stakes being so high for the Newcastle side.
The loss came in front of their home fans, on old boys' day and jeopardised their chances of hosting a home final by finishing the regular season at fifth or sixth place on the ladder.
Plenty at stake for both teams with finals fast approaching.

Jett Cleary is set to make his NRL debut in the halves following the late withdrawal of Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita, the Warriors have confirmed.
The 21-year-old, who is the brother of Penrith playmaker Nathan Cleary , has been playing in the club’s NSW Cup this season as he awaits his opportunity to play in first grade. He is now set to debut against the Knights.
Jett Cleary seen in action for the Warriors in the NSW Cup Getty
The Warriors said the club did not want to “risk the established halves” due to their injury concerns so close to the finals series.
Martin had been named to return from a hamstring injury that kept him on the sidelines for the last three weeks. Harris-Tavita also has a hamstring concern.
Both are expected to complete all training sessions in the coming weeks and be ready for a likely home qualifying final.
Cleary will, however, move into the halves alongside Luke Hanson.
“He is a great kid. He left his home as an 18-year-old to ply his trade abroad,” Penrith great Mark Geyer said of Cleary’s debut on 2GB’s Continous Call Team .
“He is a lot like his brother who is an astute student of the game.

items.snippet: Webby and the Jett: Cleary set for Warriors debut against Knights    NZ Herald
items.body_excerpt:
Warriors v Knights, NRL round 26, 4pm, Sunday, August 30, at Go Media Mt Smart, Auckland.
New Zealand Warriors coach Andrew Webster has had to call on youth after being forced to make late changes to the starting halves in their clash with Newcastle in Auckland tomorrow.
Halfback Jett Cleary will make his NRL debut starting in the No 23 jumper. He replaces Te Maire Martin, who was set to return from a hamstring injury but has been withdrawn from the squad.
He’ll be joined in the halves by a familiar face, with fellow reserve-grade regular Luke Hanson starting at five-eighth after Chanel Harris-Tavita (hamstring) was also ruled out.
While Martin and Harris-Tavita have been withdrawn from Sunday’s clash, they will both train fully next week to line up in the final regular season match against Manly next Saturday (September 5).
The changes come as the Warriors set out to retain top spot on the NRL ladder heading into the final round of the season.
Their 45-26 win over the South Sydney Rabbitohs last week moved them to the top of the standings, but Penrith’s 24-10 victory over the Canterbury Bulldogs on Friday has put the pressure back on.
The Warriors must now beat the Knights by at least 14 points to reclaim top spot and go into the last round as the competition’s No 1 side.
However, it won’t be easy against the Knights, who will have plenty to play for in their final regular-season match after being allocated the bye next week. A win would go a long way towards securing a home elimination final.
They also possess one of the NRL’s most dangerous attacking weapons in Kalyn Ponga , who can break a game open in an instant.
Should the Warriors finish on top, it would be the second time in the club’s history they have claimed the J.J. Giltinan Shield, joining the 2002 side as the only Warriors teams to finish the regular season as minor premiers.
But despite the opportunity to make a bit of club history, coach Andrew Webster insists finishing top of the ladder is not occupying the Warriors’ minds .
“We’ve never mentioned it once,” Webster said.
“We’ve just got to worry about chasing our best game. If we chase our best game the next two weeks, that guarantees us top two. If it doesn’t, then we’ll just deal with whatever situation comes.
“But chasing minor premierships isn’t the top of our list at the moment. It has not been mentioned.”

Ali Leiataua also returns to the starting side at centre, pushing Adam Pompey back to the bench, while Morgan Gannon has been named among the reserves.
